text: Men used to go to war and now they sell b2b SaaS
i KNOW SaaS stands for software as a service but that will not stop me from checking stripe 40 times a day even though nothing changed
the most annoying part of running a business for me is collecting receipts for my accountant

I'm 30. I built an AI startup to $4.3M ARR. Got accepted into YC.

Here's exactly what I'd do from zero:

I spent 18 months building features nobody asked for.

Then I deleted 80% of my product.

MRR went up 3x.

AI makes everyone a writer.

But it doesn't make everyone interesting.

The bottleneck moved from output to insight.
nobody talks about how most 'career growth' is just switching companies every 2 years
every indie hacker i talk to is making $0 and calling it 'pre-revenue'

Remote work isn't a perk.

It's a trade-off.

You save 2 hours of commute but lose 2 hours of social capital.

Know which one you need.

Tests don't catch bugs.

They document your assumptions.

If your assumptions are wrong, your tests just confirm the wrong behavior faster.

I raised $2M and built the wrong product.

My friend bootstrapped the right one with $0.

18 months later:
Me: $0 MRR, $200k left
Him: $40k MRR, profitable, solo

I went to the gym for 365 days straight.

Here's what nobody tells you:

Day 1-30: motivation
Day 31-180: discipline
Day 181+: identity

You don't rise to your goals. You fall to your identity.
nobody talks about how the first 20 minutes of a workout are a negotiation with yourself and the last 10 are a negotiation with god

I lost 40lbs in 6 months.

No keto. No intermittent fasting. No personal trainer.

I just stopped drinking my calories.

That's it. That's the whole secret.
the gym is the only place where you pay $40/month to torture yourself and somehow that's the best decision you'll ever make

your body is the only place you have to live.

stop treating it like a rental.

I tracked every workout for a year.

The days I felt weak were the days I got strongest.

The days I felt strong were the days I got injured.

Listen to your body, not your ego.

running teaches you one thing:

the voice that says 'stop' comes way before your body actually needs to stop.

that gap is where growth lives.

I paid off $87,000 in debt in 2 years.

Not from a side hustle.
Not from crypto.
Not from a rich uncle.

I just stopped buying things I couldn't afford.

Revolutionary concept, I know.
the stock market is the only place where everything is on sale and everyone runs out of the store
nobody talks about how 'building credit' is just training yourself to borrow money you don't have so a bank can charge you 24% later

I invested $500/month into index funds for 10 years.

Total invested: $60,000
Final balance: $112,000

I didn't pick stocks. I didn't time the market. I just didn't stop.

Boring works.
every 'financial expert' on here is selling a course about how to make money by selling courses about how to make money

the best financial advice I ever got:

live like you're broke for 5 years so you can live like you're rich for 50.

everyone wants the second part without the first.

I cooked dinner every night for 30 days.

Here's what happened:

- saved $600 on takeout
- lost 8lbs without trying
- my kids actually eat vegetables now

the secret was just... doing it.
nobody talks about how cooking is the only skill where you mess up 50 times and people still eat it and say 'thanks'

a recipe is just a suggestion.

the best cooks I know don't measure anything.

they taste, adjust, taste again.

that's the whole skill.

I tried 15 meal prep recipes in one month.

12 were terrible.
3 were decent.
0 were as good as the TikTok said they'd be.

Here's the 3 that actually worked 👇

I traveled to 30 countries solo.

Here's what nobody tells you:

Day 3 is always the worst. You'll want to go home.

Push through day 3. Everything after that is magic.

the best travel advice I ever got:

don't plan your itinerary. plan your first 2 nights. the rest figures itself out.
nobody talks about how the best part of traveling isn't the places, it's the version of yourself you become when nobody knows your name

I spent $4000 on a 2-week trip to Japan.

$1200 was flights.
$800 was food.
$500 was trains.
$1500 was mistakes I won't make next time.

Here's how to do it for $2500 👇

I read 100 books in one year.

Here's the uncomfortable truth:

I remember maybe 15 of them.

The value isn't in remembering. It's in the thinking the books forced me to do.
nobody talks about how reading 50 books a year is just procrastination with a more socially acceptable label

the best books I've ever read were all recommended by someone I respected, not by an algorithm.

your taste is shaped by your circle. choose both carefully.

I tried 12 productivity apps in one year.

Here's what I found 👇

I quit my $180k job to start a YouTube channel.

Year 1: $0
Year 2: $340/month
Year 3: $22k/month

Here's what I wish I knew on day 1 👇
nobody talks about how the first 50 videos you make will be terrible and that's not a bug, it's the curriculum

every YouTuber I know who blew up did one thing:

they posted every week for 2 years before anyone noticed.

everyone wants the blow up. nobody wants the 2 years.

I posted on TikTok every day for 90 days.

Day 1-30: 12 views average
Day 31-60: 200 views average
Day 61-90: one hit 2.3M

the algorithm didn't change. I just got less boring.

I edited 1000 videos in 3 years.

Here's the secret nobody tells you:

The first 3 seconds matter more than the next 3 minutes.

If they don't stop scrolling, your edit doesn't exist.
nobody talks about how editing is 90% watching the same clip 40 times until you hate it, and that's how you know it's good

the best editors I know don't use fancy transitions.

they use jump cuts, sound design, and pacing.

everything else is decoration.

decoration doesn't retain viewers. pacing does.

I ran raw footage through my retention editing software and the editor's reaction was priceless.

He gave me his footage. I ran it through the tool. He watched the final cut.

Now he's an affiliate and we're both making money.

Here's how the deal works 👇

every editor I reach out to says the same thing:

'I don't need software, I have my workflow.'

Then I show them what retention editing does to their raw footage.

They change their mind in 30 seconds.

Show, don't tell.

I offered 5 pro editors a deal:

give me your raw footage
I run it through my retention software
you react to the final cut
you get affiliate + free subscription

3 said yes in 48 hours.

Here's the exact pitch 👇

I wrote every day for a year.

Here's what happened:

- first 90 days: garbage
- day 91-180: less garbage
- day 181+: people started sharing my stuff

the secret was just not stopping.
nobody talks about how writing is just thinking on paper, and most people can't write because they can't think clearly, not because they can't spell

the best writing advice I ever got:

write like you're explaining it to a smart friend who doesn't know the topic.

not a child. not a professor. a smart friend.

that's the sweet spot.

I designed 500 logos in 2 years.

Here's what I learned:

90% of 'bad design' is just too many ideas fighting for attention.

Pick one idea. Kill the rest. Ship it.
nobody talks about how design trends are just peer pressure with better typography

good design is invisible.

bad design is the only kind you notice.

if someone compliments your design, ask them what specifically.

if they can't answer, it's probably bad.

I sold my house without a realtor.

Saved $24,000 in commission.

Here's how 👇
nobody talks about how buying a house is the only time you'll spend $400,000 and the seller will negotiate over a $2000 repair

the best real estate advice I ever got:

don't buy the best house on the block. buy the worst house on the best block.

you can fix a house. you can't fix a neighborhood.

I've been in therapy for 3 years.

Here's the thing nobody tells you:

Therapy doesn't fix you. It gives you tools to fix yourself.

The work happens between sessions, not during them.
nobody talks about how 'self-care' became buying bath bombs instead of actually dealing with why you're stressed

anxiety isn't fear of the future.

it's fear that you won't be able to handle the future.

the fix isn't certainty. it's self-trust.

you've survived 100% of your bad days. act like it.

I've been married for 12 years.

Here's the secret:

It's not about finding the right person. It's about being the right person.

Everyone focuses on the first half. Nobody does the second.
nobody talks about how the hardest part of a long relationship isn't the big fights, it's choosing each other on the boring tuesdays

I homeschooled my kids for 4 years.

Here's what nobody tells you:

The hardest part isn't teaching them. It's unlearning how you were taught.

Your kids aren't broken. The system you compare them to is.
nobody talks about how parenting is the only job where you get zero training, zero feedback, and the performance review happens 20 years later

I played 2000 hours of one video game.

Here's what I learned about skill:

The pros don't do fancy things. They do the basics perfectly, every time, under pressure.

Fancy loses to consistent. Always.
nobody talks about how gaming taught more people about teamwork, leadership, and communication than any corporate training ever did

I produced music for 10 years with zero hits.

Then I stopped trying to sound like everyone else and started making what I actually listened to.

6 months later: 2 million streams.

Here's what changed 👇
nobody talks about how the best musicians aren't the most talented, they're the ones who didn't quit during the 5 years nobody cared

I took 10,000 photos in one year.

Here's what I learned:

10 were good.
2 were great.
0 were as good as I thought they were when I took them.

Your taste develops faster than your skill. That gap is called growth.

the best camera is the one you have on you.

the best lens is the one you know how to use.

the best light is the one you didn't plan for.

stop buying gear. start taking photos.

I started a podcast 2 years ago.

Episode 1: 12 downloads (5 were my mom)
Episode 100: 40,000 downloads per episode

Here's the only thing that mattered 👇
nobody talks about how the best podcasters aren't the best interviewers, they're the best listeners who happen to have a microphone

I ran 5 cold email campaigns. Here's what worked:

1. Personalized first line (not 'love your content')
2. One specific reason I'm reaching out
3. One clear ask
4. Zero fluff

Reply rate went from 2% to 23%.
nobody talks about how 'following up' isn't annoying, it's respectful. you're reminding them of something they said they cared about and forgot.

I reached out to 50 creators with a partnership offer.

48 ignored me.
2 said yes.

Those 2 made me $40k.

Stop counting the no's. Start counting the yes's.

I spent $50,000 on ads before I learned this:

The ad isn't the problem. The landing page isn't the problem. The offer is the problem.

Fix the offer first. Everything else is a multiplier on a broken base.
nobody talks about how 'going viral' is just making something so specific that a small group of people feel seen, and that small group shares it with everyone they know

the best marketing I've ever seen was a customer explaining the product to another customer.

you can't buy that. you can only build something worth explaining.

I've been meditating for 1000 days straight.

Here's what nobody tells you:

It doesn't make you calm. It makes you aware.

Awareness of chaos isn't calm. But it's better than being asleep in it.
nobody talks about how meditation is the only thing you do by doing nothing and somehow it's the hardest thing you'll ever try

I learned 3 languages in 5 years.

Here's the secret:

Don't study the language. Use the language.

10 minutes of actually using it beats 2 hours of studying it.

Every. Single. Time.
nobody talks about how the best way to learn a language is to date someone who speaks it and tolerate the awkward silences

I've been journaling for 5 years.

Here's what I learned reading them back:

My problems didn't change. My perspective on them did.

That's the whole point.
nobody talks about how journaling is just arguing with yourself but the other side actually has to listen

I built a personal brand from 0 to 50k followers in 8 months.

No ads. No viral posts. No threads.

I just answered the same question every day for 8 months.

Consistency is a cheat code nobody wants to use.
nobody talks about how 'building a personal brand' is just becoming known for something specific and repeating it until strangers mention your name

I launched a product 3 times before it worked.

Launch 1: 0 customers
Launch 2: 3 customers
Launch 3: 300 customers

The product didn't change. The audience did.

I stopped selling to people who didn't want it.
nobody talks about how 'product-market fit' isn't something you find, it's something you notice after you've already been doing it for 6 months

I've been vegan for 5 years.

Here's what nobody tells you:

The food part is easy. The social part is hard.

Every dinner party is a negotiation you didn't sign up for.
nobody talks about how the best diet isn't keto, vegan, or paleo. it's the one you'll actually stick to for more than 3 weeks

I trained my dog in 30 days.

Here's the secret:

The dog wasn't the problem. I was the problem.

Dogs don't need training. Owners do.
nobody talks about how getting a dog teaches you more about consistency than any self-help book because the dog doesn't accept your excuses

I switched from coffee to green tea for 30 days.

Here's what happened:

- no afternoon crash
- slept 1 hour deeper
- stopped getting jittery
- my dentist stopped yelling at me

the caffeine wasn't the problem. the 4 cups were.
nobody talks about how sleep is the only productivity hack that's free, proven, and nobody does it because it's boring

I started a newsletter 6 months ago.

0 subscribers → 12,000 subscribers.

No paid ads. No viral threads. No celebrity shoutouts.

Here's the exact playbook 👇
nobody talks about how the best newsletters aren't written, they're curated. and curation is just caring about a topic more than your readers have time to

I negotiated my salary from $95k to $140k in one conversation.

Here's what I said 👇
nobody talks about how the biggest salary jumps don't come from promotions, they come from switching companies, because loyalty is taxed at ~30%

I've been sober for 2 years.

Here's what nobody tells you:

Quitting isn't the hard part. Explaining why you quit to people who are uncomfortable with their own drinking is the hard part.
nobody talks about how 'just one drink' is the most expensive lie in the english language

I built an audience on LinkedIn from 0 to 30k in 6 months.

Here's the secret:

I stopped writing for everyone and started writing for the person I was 3 years ago.

Specific beats broad. Always.
nobody talks about how LinkedIn is just corporate Twitter where everyone pretends their failures were intentional

I started a side hustle while working full-time.

Year 1: $200/month
Year 2: $2000/month
Year 3: quit my job, $15k/month

Here's what nobody tells you about the gap between year 2 and 3 👇
nobody talks about how 'passive income' is just income you built actively for 3 years before it started paying you while you sleep

I've been doing standup comedy for 5 years.

Here's what I learned about writing:

The laugh isn't in the punchline. It's in the setup.

If the setup is perfect, the punchline writes itself. If the setup is weak, no punchline can save it.
nobody talks about how comedy is the only profession where you get instant feedback and most people still ignore it because they think the audience is wrong

I taught myself to code in 12 months.

No bootcamp. No CS degree. No mentor.

Here's what actually worked 👇
nobody talks about how the hardest part of learning to code isn't the syntax, it's accepting that you'll feel stupid for 6 months before you feel competent

the best programmers I know don't memorize algorithms.

they know how to break a problem into smaller problems.

that's the whole skill. everything else is googleable.

I ran a marathon in under 4 hours after 6 months of training.

Here's what nobody tells you:

The marathon isn't hard. The 5am runs in the rain are hard.

The marathon is just the receipt.
nobody talks about how running a marathon is 90% mental and the other 10% is convincing yourself to sign up

I've been investing in crypto for 5 years.

Here's what I learned:

The technology matters less than the community.

The community matters less than the liquidity.

And none of it matters if you can't hold through a 80% drawdown.
nobody talks about how everyone's a genius in a bull market and the real test is whether you're still here in the bear market

I built a SaaS tool for editors.

Reached out to 20 pro editors.

Offered: raw footage → my retention software → they react → affiliate + free sub.

5 said yes. 3 are now power users.

Here's the exact outreach script 👇

the best outreach I ever sent wasn't a pitch.

It was: 'I love your work. I built something that might make it better. Want to see it?'

No ask. No offer. Just curiosity.

The offer came after they said yes.

I offered a creator an affiliate deal.

They said: 'I don't promote things I haven't used.'

I said: 'That's why I'm giving it to you for free first.'

They signed up in 10 minutes.

Remove the risk. The deal closes itself.

I've been doing SEO for 10 years.

Here's the truth:

SEO isn't dead. It's just harder.

And harder means the people who were faking it are gone, and the people who actually care about the user are finally winning.
nobody talks about how the best SEO strategy is to write something so good that people link to it without being asked

I've been a freelancer for 4 years.

Here's what I learned:

The clients who negotiate your rate the hardest are the ones who pay the latest.

The clients who pay your full rate without blinking pay on day 1.

Price is a filter, not a barrier.
nobody talks about how freelancing isn't freedom, it's just trading one boss for ten bosses who all think they're your only client

I've been doing cold outreach for 3 years.

Here's the #1 mistake:

You're writing the message you'd want to receive.

But you're not the recipient. They are.

Write the message THEY would want to receive. Not you.

I sent 1000 cold DMs last year.

Here's what worked:

- 2 sentences max
- one specific compliment (not 'love your content')
- one specific question
- zero pitch

Reply rate: 34%.

The pitch comes after they reply.

I built a community from 0 to 5000 members in 90 days.

No ads. No influencers. No giveaways.

Here's the secret:

I welcomed every single person by name and asked them one question.

That's it. People stay where they feel seen.
nobody talks about how the best communities don't grow, they compound. and compounding looks like nothing is happening until suddenly everyone knows about it

I've been teaching online for 3 years.

Here's what I learned:

People don't pay for information. They pay for transformation.

Information is free. The path from A to B is not.

Sell the path, not the map.
nobody talks about how the best teachers aren't the smartest people, they're the people who remember what it was like to not understand

I've been doing public speaking for 10 years.

Here's the secret:

Nobody remembers what you said. They remember how you made them feel.

So stop memorizing your slides and start caring about your audience.

nobody talks about how the fear of public speaking isn't fear of speaking, it's fear of being judged. and the audience isn't judging you, they're hoping you're good so they don't have to sit through something awkward

I've been doing email marketing for 8 years.

Here's the truth:

The subject line matters more than the email.

Because if they don't open it, your email doesn't exist.

Spend 50% of your time on the subject line. I'm not joking.
nobody talks about how the best email marketers don't sell in the email. they sell in the P.S. because that's where the eyes go when the body says no

I've been a nurse for 15 years.

Here's what nobody tells you:

The hardest part isn't the hours. It's watching people make the same choices that put them in the hospital.

You can't care more about someone's health than they do.
nobody talks about how healthcare workers don't need thoughts and prayers, they need staffing ratios and lunch breaks

I've been a teacher for 20 years.

Here's what I learned:

The students who succeed aren't the smartest. They're the ones who ask for help.

Asking for help isn't weakness. It's the most underrated skill in the world.
nobody talks about how teachers don't burn out from teaching. they burn out from the 40% of the job that has nothing to do with teaching

I've been doing sales for 15 years.

Here's the truth:

Closing isn't a technique. It's a consequence.

If you've done the first 90% right, the close is just the natural next step.

If you're struggling to close, you didn't mess up the close. You messed up the 90%.
nobody talks about how the best salespeople aren't pushy, they're patient. and patience in sales looks like losing deals you could have forced, to win deals you actually deserve

I started a YouTube channel about cooking.

0 subscribers → 100k in 14 months.

Here's what nobody tells you:

The algorithm doesn't pick winners. It picks patterns.

I posted the same pattern every week for 14 months. The algorithm finally noticed.
nobody talks about how the first 100 subscribers are harder than the next 100,000 because you're fighting for strangers' attention with zero proof you deserve it
